forks.purpose: Desktop previs tool for AI filmmaking. You stage grey-box 3D scenes (people, vehicles, 50+ environment kits), choreograph camera and actor movement on a marks-based timeline, then export a deterministic motion-reference package (MP4, depth and normal passes, stills, per-generator prompt, ComfyUI workflow, metadata.json) for AI video generators (Seedance 2.0, Veo 3.1, Kling, LTX 2.3, Wan 2.2). It also has a built-in MCP server so Claude Code can drive the running app.

features.name: Stage / Shoot / Deliver modes
features.description: Three-mode app (type Mode = 'stage'|'shoot'|'deliver' in src/renderer/store.ts, switch in App.tsx titlebar). Stage places assets, Shoot adds marks and a timeline, Deliver exports.

features.name: Asset library
features.description: Procedural grey-box people, animals, vehicles, furniture, props and 50+ environment kits. Catalog in src/engine/assets.ts (290 lines), meshes built in code in src/renderer/viewport/builders.ts (6252 lines). Emoji thumbnails (thumbFor in Library.tsx), no image assets. Custom 3D model import via importAsset.

features.name: Marks-based choreography
features.description: Actor and camera marks on a shared timeline with per-mark easing, gaits, and speed sanity warnings. Pure engine: src/engine/evaluate.ts (state(t)), path.ts, gaits.ts, easing.ts.

features.name: Camera system
features.description: Real sensor and lens math (src/engine/camera.ts), rigs (dolly, steadicam, handheld, crane, drone, car-mount in rigs.ts), 39 camera moves (camera-moves.ts, 1498 lines), auto-framing (2S, OTS, REV, TOP, LOW, DUTCH), look-through mode, aspect masks, rack focus.

features.name: Motion library
features.description: 194 single-performer character motions across fight/dance/gesture/everyday/sport/stunt (src/engine/motions.ts, 9575 lines) and 33 action-path presets for planes, helicopters, cars, horses and debris (action-presets.ts).

features.name: Choreography engine and crowds
features.description: buildRoutine() in src/engine/choreography.ts makes seeded dance, fight and chase routines (formations, canon, mirror, endings). src/engine/sequences.ts spawns 2-60 person crowds. UI is the Choreographer panel in Library.tsx.

features.name: 3D scan import
features.description: Gaussian-splat environments (.ply/.splat/.spz/.ksplat) via @mkkellogg/gaussian-splats-3d. Editor-only, never rendered into exports, and listed in metadata.json.

features.name: Lighting and sky
features.description: 9 lighting presets, three of them driven by a three.js Sky dome (SceneManager.ts).

features.name: Coverage model
features.description: A scene owns the blocking and each shot owns a camera. ProjectRail lists scenes and shots, with draft shots and duplicate/reorder.

features.name: Deterministic export
features.description: Frame loop in src/renderer/export/exporter.ts. Pipes raw RGBA to ffmpeg for the clean, depth and normal passes. Also writes stills at each mark, a top-down diagram, prompt.txt, comfyui-workflow.json (comfy.ts), metadata.json and README.txt. Also does animatic stitching (ffmpeg concat), contact sheet, and glTF/Blender handoff (gltf.ts).

features.name: Generator profiles
features.description: Data-driven profiles in src/engine/profiles.ts (BUILTIN_PROFILES) and prompt generation in src/engine/prompt.ts. The Deliver dropdown reads from this list.

features.name: Reference underlay
features.description: Ghost or PiP reference video synced to the timeline (ReferenceUnderlay.tsx). Fed by the set_reference control action, which Motion Previs Studio uses for its handoff.

features.name: AI reference analysis
features.description: src/main/analyze.ts sends an image or video frame to Claude (@anthropic-ai/sdk, structured output) and returns an entity/lighting/camera layout. Auth comes from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an `ant auth login` profile. Triggered from src/renderer/ai/populate.ts.

features.name: Stage presets
features.description: Global reusable stagings stored in the config dir (src/main/presets.ts, IPC presets:*).

features.name: Take bar, spike-tape marks, coach, Help
features.description: Rehearse/Record/Review take bar in Viewport.tsx, BlockingCoach and a tabbed HelpOverlay in Help.tsx (772 lines).

features.name: Autosave and recovery
features.description: 60s autosave to .autosave/project.autosave.json. On open, a newer backup is offered back.

features.name: MCP agent control
features.description: mcp/blockout-mcp.mjs (zero-dep stdio server) -> localhost HTTP control server (src/main/control.ts) -> IPC -> src/renderer/control/handler.ts. About 30 tools including get_state, add_entity, add_actor_mark, add_camera_mark, apply_framing, spawn_choreography, import_scan, screenshot, export_shot, set_reference.

screens.name: Welcome
screens.description: Logo (assets/logo.png at 260px), tagline, New Project, Open Project and Tutorial buttons, Credits block with required attribution links.

screens.name: App shell and titlebar
screens.description: 44px titlebar with traffic-light inset on macOS, BLOCKOUT wordmark, project name with dirty dot, STAGE/SHOOT/DELIVER segmented switch (.mode-switch), Save, ? Help. Global keyboard map (undo/redo/save/space/M/C/?/Esc/1-9) lives here.

screens.name: Stage layout
screens.description: .main grid 200px | 1fr | 264px. Left: ProjectRail + Library (search, category grid, Sequences, Choreographer, Stage Presets, Populate-from-reference) + compact Credits. Center: Viewport. Right: Inspector.

screens.name: Shoot layout
screens.description: Same grid plus a resizable Timeline under the viewport (457 lines): ruler, playhead, per-entity Lane tracks with .mark-pill items, warning chips.

screens.name: Deliver layout
screens.description: .deliver-layout grid 1fr | 380px. Viewport preview on black, plus a panel with generator select, pass toggles (Clean/Depth/Normal), labels mode, resolution, generated prompt box, progress bar, and animatic/contact-sheet/Blender buttons.

screens.name: Viewport (WebGL)
screens.description: Canvas plus React overlays: HUD (lens, aspect, marks/paths eye toggles), ShotSizeRow, FramingRow, TakeBar, GizmoModeRow, thirds grid, placement and mark hints, empty state. Gizmo uses three.js TransformControls and ViewHelper.

screens.name: Reference underlay and controls
screens.description: Video overlay and PiP with opacity and mode controls.

screens.name: Inspector (context-sensitive)
screens.description: Variants selected by store Selection: SceneInspector/ShotSection, EntityInspector, MultiEntityInspector, CameraInspector (CameraPoseSection, CameraMovesSection), MarkInspector, MultiMarkInspector, ScanInspector/ScansSection, plus AnimateTab, MotionPresetsSection, ActionPresetsSection, PoseSection, MarriageSection, GroupAnimateSection.

screens.name: Help overlay
screens.description: Modal (.help-modal/.help-v4) with tabs, searchable how-do-I tasks, card grid and keyboard grid. BlockingCoach is a floating step checklist.

screens.name: Toasts
screens.description: info/error/success toast stack (.toast).

screens.name: Native dialogs (not renderer UI)
screens.description: New project (save dialog), open project (folder dialog), pick file. All are Electron native dialogs.

stack.shell: Electron 43 (package.json). Main in src/main/index.ts, preload in src/preload/index.ts (contextBridge exposes window.blockout), renderer in src/renderer. electron-builder produces the DMG and NSIS installers.
stack.ui: React 18 + TypeScript strict. No component library, no router. Function components with a zustand store. Plain CSS in src/renderer/styles.css (689 lines) plus many inline styles. Entry is src/renderer/index.html -> main.tsx -> App.tsx.
stack.state: zustand v5 in src/renderer/store.ts (1225 lines). One store owns doc, selection, playback, undo and toasts. All doc mutations go through store.mutate(label, fn). A tiny pub/sub in bus.ts carries viewport events such as emit('setLens'). The store is also exposed as window.__blockout.
stack.rendering3d: three 0.170 (WebGLRenderer, OrbitControls, TransformControls, ViewHelper, Sky) plus @mkkellogg/gaussian-splats-3d. SceneManager.ts owns all three.js code; Viewport.tsx is the React wrapper. Exports render offscreen and read back with gl.readPixels.
stack.build: electron-vite 6 beta + Vite 8 + @vitejs/plugin-react. Aliases @engine and @renderer. Vitest 4 for unit tests, Playwright for e2e against the built app. ESLint 9. Node 22.

styling.approach: Plain CSS custom properties in one global stylesheet (src/renderer/styles.css, 168 var(--) uses). Components use semantic class names (.btn, .seg, .panel, .field, .rail-*, .mark-pill, .help-*). Roughly 160 inline style={{}} objects in TSX also reference the vars (Inspector 69, Library 33, Viewport 17, DeliverPanel 12, Help 15, Timeline 8, App 4, ReferenceUnderlay 3, ProjectRail 1). No Tailwind, CSS modules or CSS-in-JS.

desktopOnly.mechanism: Main-process fs via IPC project:save, project:saveBackup, project:load. A project is a .blockout folder holding project.json, assets/, scans/, refs/, exports/, .autosave/. Native dialogs: dialog:newProject, dialog:openProject, dialog:pickFile.
desktopOnly.webFallback: File System Access API (showDirectoryPicker) on Chromium for the same folder layout. Safari and Firefox have no equivalent, so they would need an IndexedDB/OPFS project or zip import/export. Autosave to OPFS works in all browsers.

desktopOnly.mechanism: IPC project:importAsset, scan:import, project:importReference copy files into the project folder. file:readAbsolute reads them back as ArrayBuffer with a path-escape check (readProjectFile).
desktopOnly.webFallback: File input or drop, then store blobs in OPFS or IndexedDB, or write into the picked directory handle. SceneManager and ReferenceUnderlay only need ArrayBuffer/blob URLs.

desktopOnly.mechanism: export:begin spawns ffmpeg (libx264, crf 18, yuv420p) and export:frame writes raw RGBA to stdin. Also export:end, export:cancel (process-tree kill), export:concat (animatic) and export:writeFile. ffmpeg is resolved by src/main/ffmpeg.ts (BLOCKOUT_FFMPEG env, packaged binary, Homebrew paths, PATH).
desktopOnly.webFallback: Two options. WebCodecs VideoEncoder plus an MP4 muxer (mp4-muxer) in the browser, or ffmpeg.wasm. Either one likely breaks the byte-identical-output guarantee that the smoke test checks (the AGENTS.md hard rule), because encoder output differs. A Vercel web build would also need Vercel Functions or a worker for any server-side ffmpeg, which does not suit large raw frames.

desktopOnly.mechanism: export:writeFile writes prompt.txt, metadata.json, comfyui-workflow.json, stills and glTF to absolute paths. showFolder reveals the result in Finder or Explorer (shell:showFolder).
desktopOnly.webFallback: Download a zip (fflate/JSZip) or write through the File System Access API. 'Reveal in Finder' has no web equivalent.

desktopOnly.feature: MCP control server and discovery file
desktopOnly.mechanism: src/main/control.ts runs an HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 (random port, bearer token). It writes ~/.config/blockout/control.json (APPDATA on Windows). mcp/blockout-mcp.mjs is a separate Node stdio bridge that relays to the renderer via IPC control:invoke/control:result. Handler is src/renderer/control/handler.ts.
desktopOnly.webFallback: A browser tab cannot open a listening socket. It would need a small local relay (WebSocket to a Node bridge) or a hosted relay. Pure web deploy on Vercel would lose agent control unless this is redesigned. handler.ts itself is renderer code and is reusable.

desktopOnly.mechanism: src/main/analyze.ts calls @anthropic-ai/sdk in the main process. Auth comes from env or `ant auth login`. For video it extracts a frame with ffmpeg.
desktopOnly.webFallback: A Vercel Function proxy holding ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (the key must stay server-side). Video frames can come from a <video> canvas grab instead of ffmpeg.

desktopOnly.mechanism: src/main/presets.ts reads and writes JSON in ~/.config/blockout/presets (IPC presets:list/save/load/delete).
desktopOnly.webFallback: IndexedDB or localStorage.

desktopOnly.mechanism: preload computes PlatformInfo (modifier key glyphs, 'Reveal in Finder' label). shell:openExternal only allows https hosts wassermanproductions.com and wasserman.ai.
desktopOnly.webFallback: navigator.platform checks and window.open.

desktopOnly.mechanism: hiddenInset titlebar on macOS, app-region drag CSS, 84px left padding for traffic lights, Menu removed on non-Mac.
desktopOnly.webFallback: Drop the drag region and the padding.

webBuild.existingWebConfig: None. electron.vite.config.ts defines only main/preload/renderer for Electron. The renderer has root src/renderer and its own index.html, so a plain Vite web config with the same aliases (@engine, @renderer) and a build-time define for the three __BLOCKOUT_* constants would build it. There is no vercel.json and no web target in CI.
webBuild.notes: The renderer is nearly pure browser code. The only desktop coupling is window.blockout (typed in src/preload/index.ts, declared in src/renderer/global.d.ts), about 20 methods used from 12 renderer files. A web-shim object implementing BlockoutAPI would cover everything. Easy parts: dialogs, file import, save/load (File System Access or OPFS), presets, platform info. Hard parts: (1) ffmpeg export, which needs WebCodecs or ffmpeg.wasm and loses the byte-determinism guarantee, (2) the MCP control server, which needs a socket, (3) analyze.ts, which needs a server proxy. src/renderer/index.html has a CSP that references a blockout-media: scheme that is never registered anywhere in src, so it is dead config. The CSP uses 'wasm-unsafe-eval' for splats and worker-src blob:. A Vercel deployment needs matching headers or a relaxed CSP. App.tsx reads window.blockout.platform at module top level (PLATFORM_CLASS), so the shim must be installed before React imports. Min window is 1100x700 and body is overflow:hidden, so it is desktop-sized with no responsive layout beyond one @media (max-width: 620px) rule for Help. Recommended path: a thin web shim (src/renderer/web-shim.ts), Chromium-first, export via WebCodecs for preview-quality MP4 plus zip packaging, keep full-fidelity export on desktop.

importsFrom: Motion Previs Studio: its MCP tool send_to_blockout (and its electron/blockoutProtocol.cjs, config.cjs) hands a reference/depth/pose clip to a running Blockout via the control server. Blockout receives it through set_reference with handoffVersion 1 (src/renderer/control/handler.ts line ~607, copied into refs/ as a ghost or PIP underlay). Capabilities advertised in control.json: ['health','rpc','set_reference','motion-handoff-v1'].
Stage presets and project folders (.blockout) are local to Blockout and not shared with the other tools.
exportsTo: AI video generators via the shot package (reference mp4, depth mp4, normal mp4, stills, prompt.txt, metadata.json).
Blender (animated camera .glb plus an import script, from export/gltf.ts).
Animatic MP4 (ffmpeg concat) and a contact sheet PNG.
fileFormats: project.json (pretty-printed, stable-key-order, schema in src/engine/schema.ts and types.ts)
interop.mcp: mcp/blockout-mcp.mjs, a zero-dependency Node >=18 stdio server. Register with: claude mcp add blockout -- node /ABS/PATH/mcp/blockout-mcp.mjs. It reads the control.json descriptor (protocol v1, also legacy unversioned) in ~/.config/blockout, or %APPDATA%\blockout on Windows, and posts to /rpc with a bearer token. Only works while the app is running. This is the same descriptor pattern Motion Previs Studio reads (its config.cjs lists Blockout control.json candidates).

uxIssues.issue: Fixed desktop layout. body, html and #root are overflow:hidden. The main grid is 200px | 1fr | 264px and the Deliver grid is 1fr | 380px, with a 1100x700 window minimum. Nothing collapses, and there is no responsive behavior apart from one rule in Help.
Inspector.tsx is a 2135-line single file with about 69 inline style objects mixed into 14 section components. Spacing, labels and rows are re-declared ad hoc, so restyling is slow and inconsistent.
Library uses emoji as asset thumbnails (thumbFor map) and 33 inline styles. This looks inconsistent across OSes and is not themeable.
Very small type scale: 9-13px, with many 10-11px labels (.panel-title 10px, .hud-label 9px, .rail-dur etc.). Low contrast --text-faint #5f5f6b on #18181b.

Accessibility gaps. user-select:none on body, custom div/button controls without roles or aria (mode switch, .seg, mark pills, rail items), no visible focus ring on buttons (only input focus border), the global keydown handler swallows keys (Space, M, C, digits) on anything but inputs, and the Help modal likely has no focus trap (not verified).

Help.tsx hard-codes fallback hex values inside var() calls, and its CSS variable names are not part of the base token set. It uses var(--panel, #16181d), var(--border-strong, #33343a) and var(--text-faint, #8a8d96). Since --panel is not defined in :root, the fallback #16181d always wins, which gives a different grey than --bg-panel.
Credits link component reimplements hover with onMouseEnter/Leave and inline color instead of CSS.
Single amber accent (#f5a524) is used for every state (active tab, selected pill, primary button, focus, hover border), so hierarchy between selected, active and primary is weak.
Empty and loading states are thin. Toasts carry most feedback, and the Library presets listing swallows errors silently (catch with a comment only).
Light theme does not exist. There is one dark palette, no prefers-color-scheme, no theme switch.

restyleRisks: Existing tokens (styles.css :root, 16 vars): --bg #111113, --bg-panel #18181b, --bg-raised #1f1f23, --bg-hover #26262b, --border #2b2b31, --border-strong #3a3a42, --text #ececf1, --text-dim #9b9ba6, --text-faint #5f5f6b, --accent #f5a524 (spike-tape amber), --accent-text #16130b, --danger #e5484d, --success #46a758, --mono 'SF Mono'..., --sans -apple-system/Inter/Segoe UI, --radius 8px. This is already a flat, semantic, var-driven system, so mapping to Nick's design system is mostly a rename or re-point of these 16 variables. Spacing, font size, shadow and z-index are not tokenized (raw px everywhere).

Hard-coded colors in CSS: 14 hex and 8 rgba literals in styles.css outside :root. Examples: rgba(17,17,19,0.82) and 0.85 (viewport toolbars and HUD, duplicates --bg with alpha), #000 for .deliver-preview, rgba(245,165,36,0.12) (accent tint), rgba(0,0,0,0.4/0.55) shadows and the modal backdrop. These need color-mix() or alpha tokens.

Colors in TSX: Inspector.tsx has 10 hex (SWATCHES array of 8 label colors #e5484d #f5a524 #46a758 #3b82f6 #a855f7 #ec4899 #14b8a6 #f97316 plus default label color #f5a524 twice), Help.tsx has 4 hex fallbacks, Timeline.tsx has 1 (#9b9ba6 default lane color), Viewport.tsx has 6 rgba. About 160 inline style={{}} objects exist across the renderer.

Entity label colors are DATA, not theme. Hex strings like '#e5484d' and '#3b82f6' are stored in project.json (Entity.label.color in engine/types.ts), written by the engine (engine/sequences.ts 3 hex, engine/choreography.ts 4 hex) and enumerated in the Claude analysis schema (src/main/analyze.ts, labelColor enum of the same 8 swatches). Changing the swatch palette must stay in sync with analyze.ts and must not rewrite saved colors.

Colors baked into exports: src/renderer/export/exporter.ts fills the contact sheet canvas with literal #111113 (bg), #ececf1 (text) and #9b9ba6 (dim). These are canvas 2D, so CSS vars do not apply. The deterministic render path must NOT change (AGENTS.md hard rule 5 and the byte-determinism smoke test).

Three.js scene colors are JS constants, not CSS: SceneManager.ts has about 54 hex literals, including editor background 0x1a1c20, grid 0x33343a/0x27282d, selection box 0xf5a524 (amber, matches --accent), camera/mark color #7dd3fc (sky blue, appears about 5 times), emissive selection tint 0x2b6cff, hemisphere light colors, and the lighting-preset table (lines ~771-780). builders.ts holds 947 hex literals for model materials. Only the editor chrome ones (grid, background, selection, mark colors) should follow the theme, and the lighting presets and model materials are exported pixels, so they must stay fixed. There is no bridge from CSS tokens to three.js today.

Dark-only app, and the viewport clear color assumes dark. A token-driven light theme would need the canvas clear color, grid and gizmo colors to switch too, and the export path to stay theme-independent.

Layout dimensions are baked into CSS and JS: titlebar 44px, traffic-light inset 84px, 200px/264px/380px column widths, and a Timeline height managed by .timeline-resizer. A design system with a different spacing scale will need these revisited.

CSS is a single global sheet with element-level selectors (button.btn, input[type='text'], select, textarea, ::-webkit-scrollbar, * {margin:0;padding:0}). Importing a component library (shadcn, Tailwind preflight, etc.) will collide with those global resets and with the .btn/.seg/.field class names. -webkit-scrollbar styling is Chromium-only (Safari will show its default scrollbars if this goes to web).
Window drag regions (-webkit-app-region) and .platform-macos padding only apply in Electron. In a web build they are inert but harmless.

Heavy logic lives in the renderer files that would be restyled: Inspector.tsx (2135 lines), Library.tsx (833), Help.tsx (772), Viewport.tsx (605). Mixing a rewrite of markup with unchanged store wiring is feasible because panels only read the zustand store and call store actions or the bus (emit), but the keyboard handler in App.tsx and the Viewport's pointer handling (SceneManager owns canvas events) must not lose focus to new overlay components.

forks.agentDocs: CLAUDE.md just points to AGENTS.md. AGENTS.md is the source of truth. Commands: npm install (Node 22+, ffmpeg needed for exports), npm run dev, build, start, typecheck (two tsconfig projects), lint (zero warnings), test (Vitest, engine only), smoke (build + Playwright e2e with a real export verified by ffprobe), package:mac, package:win. Definition of done: typecheck + lint + test green, and smoke green if you touched engine/, export/, main/ or SceneManager. Hard rules: (1) src/engine/ is PURE TypeScript with no DOM, three or Electron imports, and logic changes need unit tests in tests/unit/. (2) Determinism: nothing on the state(t) path may use unseeded Math.random(), Date.now() or frame-to-frame accumulated state, because a byte-determinism smoke test catches it. (3) All document mutations go through store.mutate(label, fn) or an existing store action, never by assigning to store.doc (breaks undo and dirty tracking). (4) Units are meters, seconds, radians, heading 0 faces -Z, models built facing -Z with origin at ground. (5) Exports must contain zero editor chrome, and SceneManager.renderFrameAt handles that. Gotchas: renderFrameAt intentionally renders twice (GL warm-up), do not 'optimize' it away. Frames go to ffmpeg as raw RGBA, vflipped, with even width and height. The live viewport loop is suspended during exports. Playwright runs against the built out/ directory. Automation surface: window.__blockout exposes the store, exportShot, etc., but is not a public API. docs/DESIGN.md is the product spec, docs/ROADMAP.md the build plan, docs/generator-profiles.md covers how to add a profile. MODIFICATIONS.md is the fork change log: derived from Blockout by Sam Wasserman, upstream base 6a85105..., Windows port by Gumbii Digital, downstream distributors should append their own changes and keep LICENSE/NOTICE/credits/CITATION.cff. There is no DESIGN token doc for the UI itself (docs/DESIGN.md is a product spec, and its UI section is not about tokens). docs/DESIGN.md names the design stance as 'dark, quiet chrome; the viewport is the star' (the comment at the top of styles.css).

forks.purpose: ScriptBreak turns a screenplay (.fountain, .fdx, .pdf, .txt) into a full production breakdown: scenes, cast, locations, tagged elements (props, wardrobe, vehicles, VFX and more), character/location/prop bibles, starter shot lists, a timeline, a project "Look" and a draft shooting schedule with Day Out of Days. It then exports self-executing Markdown "prompt packs" (video, storyboard-frame, coverage consult, script companion) with per-generator dialects, so any LLM or AI generator can be driven from the breakdown. It calls no model and holds no API keys; everything is local.

features.name: Script import and parsing
features.description: parseFountain, parseFDX (uses Final Draft's embedded scene lengths for exact page counts) and an offline PDF path (pdfExtract / screenplayFromPDF). Also accepts .spmd, .md and .scriptbreak project files. Parsing is regex-based (SLUG_RE, CHARACTER_RE, TRANSITION_RE); page counts are estimated at 54 lines per page in 1/8ths for non-FDX.

features.name: Auto-breakdown on import

forks.purpose: Slate is a prompt studio for AI filmmaking. It does not generate media. It holds the film bible (logline, world, cast, locations, props, lookbook), breaks it into scenes and shots, and lets a "brain" (Claude Code CLI, Codex CLI, or a local OpenAI-compatible model server) structure, tighten, riff and continuity-check shot prompts. forks.agentDocs: AGENTS.md is the agent guide. Definition of done: npm run build and verify:quality, verify:engines and verify:e2e green; verify:all before shipping. Control actions must run the same flow as UI clicks; changing an action means updating handler.ts, registry.ts, the mjs tool schema and mcp/README.md together. No private notes or agent markdown in the repo. MODIFICATIONS.md says this derivative adds Windows packaging by Gumbii Digital on top of upstream 4.1.0 and files carry a header comment pointing to it. minimalDS.rules: From CLAUDE.md: (1) src/styles/globals.css is the sole runtime source of truth, tokens.ts and Figma are mirrors. (3) Never write a dark-mode value in a component; it belongs in Layer 2. (4) Do not point semantic tokens at shadcn names (inversion). (5) If no token fits, add one in Layer 2 rather than reach for a palette class (example: --text-on-tooltip for the mode-invariant tooltip surface). (6) Pick motion by what moves: fast=state in place, base=short move/appear, slow=large surface enter, ambient=looping; ease-standard/enter/exit. (7) A new component ships with its co-located story in the same commit. (8) Do not quietly darken tokens to turn contrast green; propose values with ratios. (9) Variant convention: tone = neutral|info|warning|positive, variant = structural appearance. (10) Finish: verify render + interaction, test:a11y not newly red, then give a link.

cozyClayRecipe.tokenBridge: Local alias/replace-values layer, not a package import. CozyClay is vanilla CSS with its own custom-property names (--bg, --panel, --card, --line, --fg, --muted, --accent, ...). The restyle kept those names and changed only their values to Minimal DS dark-theme values, with a trailing comment naming the DS token each value came from. Missing roles were added as new local tokens (--surface-bar, --surface-sunk, --raised, --field, --line-soft, --scrim, --success/--warn/--danger). Deliberate local deviations are marked 'local' with the reason (e.g. --muted2 #8d8d96 because DS dark --text-tertiary fails 4.5:1 on surface-card at 2.29:1; accent uses the mode-invariant --accent-info blue instead of the monochrome --button-primary to preserve a blue identity; radius one step denser for 22-28px controls). Everything else in the CSS reads var(--token), so the DS can be re-synced by editing :root only. No dependency on @weeeha/ui at runtime.
cozyClayRecipe.gatesPorted: check:tokens (strict + ratchet baseline, adapted from stylesheet scope instead of tsx) and audit:contrast (4.5:1 on :root text tokens), both wired into the existing test runner (tools/run-tests.mjs via test/verify-token-gates.mjs). Not ported: story/axe a11y gate, liveness test, check:stories, ds-architecture conformance.
lessons: Land tokenisation as pixel-identical refactors BEFORE changing values, and verify each against a pre-change capture; then the value swap is a one-block diff in :root.
Keep the app's token names, change values; annotate each with the DS token it came from.
Do the audit in role-aware fashion: only rewrite a literal where the property role matches the token (background vs border vs color), leave off-role matches alone.
Add missing roles as local tokens at current values first, not by forcing a DS token that changes pixels.
Mark deviations from the DS as 'local' with the measured reason; the DS dark text-tertiary and ink-600 fail contrast on dark cards.
Anti-slop cleanup (glow, glass, gradients, transition: all, accent strips) belongs in the same restyle commit, and then lock it with the strict gate rules.
Gates need a ratchet baseline for legacy debt: strict for new categories, ratchet for raw colours, px font sizes, durations and gradients; --baseline regenerates it.
Re-pin visual tests (verify-theme/layout/pwa) and meta surfaces (theme-color, PWA manifest, letterbox) with the new --bg.

aiComponents.relationToMinimalDS: Same lineage and mostly compatible, but not a drop-in share. Minimal Design System (@weeeha/ui, github.com/weeeha/Minimal-Design-System, last commit 2026-08-11) is a token-first kit: 97 components (74 general + 23 AI, AI folder mirrors AI Elements incl. prompt-input, model-selector, code-block, queue, reasoning, conversation), shadcn style `radix-nova`, Radix (radix-ui ^1.6) with @base-ui/react also present, Storybook 10.4. Its src/styles/globals.css is the single source of truth. It has a three-tier token architecture: Layer 1 raw ramps (--base-*, --ink-*), Layer 2 semantic tokens (surface-card, text-secondary, border-hover; plus motion tokens --motion-fast/base/slow and ease-standard/enter/exit), and Layer 3 shadcn names aliased to Layer 2. Super-AI-Components uses stock shadcn neutral tokens directly. apps/docs/app/globals.css defines :root and .dark with plain oklch greys for --background, --foreground, --muted-foreground, --destructive, --sidebar-*, --chart-*, --radius 0.625rem and Geist fonts. Its gate (ds-rules) allows only shadcn CSS variables in components, with no raw color or palette classes. Overlap: both use the shadcn variable vocabulary, both ban raw hex, oklch and palette classes, both use `@custom-variant dark` with `.dark` on html, both use lucide, cva and Tailwind 4, and both share the same records-style token-gate architecture (Minimal DS PR #49 adopted Super-AI's ds-rules approach). Super-AI components should therefore render under Minimal's globals.css, because MDS Layer 3 aliases shadcn's names (--background, --muted-foreground, --destructive, --ring, --radius, --sidebar-primary, --chart-1 all exist there). Conflicts to resolve: (1) --warning and --warning-foreground are defined in Super-AI (quota-meter, credits-indicator, rate-limit-banner) but absent from MDS globals.css, so they need adding to MDS Layer 2, or those M-family components lose their near-limit state.
